name: task-flow

fileExplanations.backend/server.js: This is the Express.js application entry point. It wires up middleware, mounts the tasks and auth route modules, connects to MongoDB, and starts the HTTP server.
fileExplanations.backend/routes/tasks.routes.js: Defines REST endpoints for creating, listing, updating, and deleting tasks. Delegates business logic to the Task model and the notification service.
fileExplanations.backend/routes/auth.routes.js: Handles user signup, login, and JWT-based session issuance. Talks to the User model for credential verification.
fileExplanations.backend/models/Task.js: Mongoose schema and model for a Task, including title, status, priority, assignee, and due date fields.
fileExplanations.backend/models/User.js: Mongoose schema and model for application users, including hashed password storage.
fileExplanations.backend/services/notification.service.js: Sends email/websocket notifications when a task is assigned or its due date approaches.
fileExplanations.backend/services/scheduler.py: A Python cron-style scheduler that periodically checks for overdue tasks and triggers reminders via the notification service.
fileExplanations.frontend/src/App.jsx: Root React component; sets up routing between the login screen and the main task board.
fileExplanations.frontend/src/components/TaskBoard.tsx: Renders the kanban-style board of task columns (To Do / In Progress / Done) and handles drag-and-drop reordering.
fileExplanations.frontend/src/components/TaskCard.tsx: Renders a single task's title, priority badge, and assignee avatar within the board.
fileExplanations.frontend/src/api/client.ts: Thin fetch wrapper used by the frontend to call the backend REST API with the stored auth token attached.
fileExplanations.ml-service/app.py: A small Flask service exposing a /predict-priority endpoint used by the backend to suggest a task's priority.
fileExplanations.ml-service/priority_model.py: Loads a pre-trained scikit-learn model and exposes a predict() function used by the Flask app.

summary.overview: task-flow is a full-stack task-management application combining a React/Vite frontend, an Express.js/MongoDB backend, and a small Python/Flask microservice that predicts task priority using a pre-trained model. It's aimed at small teams who want kanban-style task tracking with basic ML-assisted prioritization.
summary.architecture: The system follows a three-tier architecture: a React SPA (frontend/) communicates over REST with an Express API (backend/), which persists data in MongoDB via Mongoose models. The backend also calls out to a separate Flask microservice (ml-service/) for priority prediction, keeping the ML dependency isolated from the main Node.js runtime. A scheduler.py cron-style job independently polls for overdue tasks.
insights: The ML priority-prediction service is decoupled as its own Flask microservice, called over HTTP - a good separation of concerns between Node and Python runtimes.
Authentication uses JWTs issued from a dedicated auth.routes.js module, separate from task-related business logic.
There is a mix of plain JavaScript (backend) and TypeScript (frontend components) - introducing TypeScript on the backend could improve type-safety consistency.
summary.techStackNarrative: Core stack: Node.js + Express.js + MongoDB (Mongoose) on the backend, React + Vite + TypeScript on the frontend, and Python + Flask + scikit-learn for the ML microservice. Containerized with Docker and docker-compose for local orchestration.

documentation:
# task-flow

## Overview
task-flow is a full-stack task-management application combining a React/Vite frontend, an Express.js/MongoDB backend, and a Python/Flask microservice for ML-assisted task-priority prediction.

## Tech Stack
- Frontend: React, Vite, TypeScript
- Backend: Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB (Mongoose)
- ML Service: Python, Flask, scikit-learn
- Infra: Docker, docker-compose

## Getting Started
1. `docker-compose up` to start MongoDB alongside the app.
2. `cd backend && npm install && npm run dev`
3. `cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev`
4. `cd ml-service && pip install -r requirements.txt && python app.py`
